stem.text: The number of bacteria in a culture is P(t) thousand, t hours after the culture is started. Suppose that \( P'(1) = -1 \). Write this statement in Leibniz notation, and state what it means.

answer_key.label: \( \left. \frac{dP}{dt} \right|_{t=1} = -1 \), so the rate of change of the number of bacteria with respect to time when t = 1 is -1 thousand bacteria per hour.

worked_solution.text: In \( P'(1) \) the function is P, the independent variable is t, and the derivative is evaluated at t = 1, so the statement is about one input only.
In Leibniz notation the same statement is \( \left. \frac{dP}{dt} \right|_{t=1} = -1 \).
It says that the rate of change of the number of bacteria with respect to time when t = 1 is -1 thousand bacteria per hour.

options.label: \( \left. \frac{dP}{dt} \right|_{t=1} = -1 \), so the rate of change of the number of bacteria with respect to time when t = 1 is -1 thousand bacteria per hour.
\( \left. \frac{dt}{dP} \right|_{t=1} = -1 \), so the rate of change of time with respect to the number of bacteria when t = 1 is -1 hours per thousand bacteria.
options.derivation: the roles of the two variables exchanged, so the derivative is read with respect to the dependent variable

options.label: \( \frac{P(1)}{1} = -1 \), so the number of bacteria divided by time when t = 1 is -1 thousand bacteria per hour.
options.derivation: the Leibniz fraction read as the quotient of the two quantities at the point

options.label: \( \frac{dP}{dt} = -1 \), so the rate of change of the number of bacteria with respect to time, the same at every t, is -1 thousand bacteria per hour.
options.derivation: the point of evaluation dropped, so a value at one input is read as the derivative function
